h: The Reward of Hearing Without the Yetzer Hara

p: וְהָיָה עֵקֶב תִּשְׁמְעוּן וְגוֹמֵר (דְּבָרִים ז, יב)
"And it will be, because you will hearken," etc. (Devarim 7:12).
בְּמִדְרַשׁ רַבָּה פָּרָשָׁה זוֹ (דְּבָרִים רַבָּה ג, א)
The Midrash Rabbah on this parashah (Devarim Rabbah 3:1)
the reward for the mitzvos?" etc.
HaKadosh Baruch Hu said to them:
I will give it to you.
From where do we know this?
From what we read in its section:
'And it will be, because you will hearken.'"
"And He will bless the fruit of your womb
and the fruit of your land," etc. (ibid. 7:13),
have nothing at all to do with Olam Haba,
Also the wording of the pasuk,
"And it will be, ekev, you will hearken,"
implies that you will hearken at the end,
whereas the Midrash explains it of the reward,
that it will be at the end.
אַךְ בֶּאֱמֶת אִיתָא (פֶּרֶק ד דְּאָבוֹת, ב)
But in truth it is found (Avos 4:2):
"The reward of a mitzvah is a mitzvah";
and this will be the reward,
And "ekev" refers to the days of Mashiach,
שֶׁאֵין בָּהֶם לֹא זְכוּת וְלֹא חוֹבָה וְכוּלֵּי
in which there is neither merit nor obligation," etc.
the yetzer hara will be uprooted from their heart,
as at the time of Matan Torah;
רַק שָׁם הָיָה לְפִי שָׁעָה לְבַד
only there it was merely for a time,
whereas then it will be forever.
That is why the Midrash opens
with the subject of keeping Shabbos:
two Shabbosos according to their halachah,
they would immediately be redeemed," etc.,
and in many places it is found
since they have not yet been redeemed,
even one Shabbos according to its halachah.
At first, when it was given to them in Alush.
From where do we know this?
'And the people rested on the seventh day.'"
Since it is written about them
it follows that they then kept Shabbos properly.
וְעַל יְדֵי זֶה זָכוּ בֶּאֱמֶת אָז
And through this they truly merited at that time
the yetzer hara returned to its place.
שֶׁמָּא לְרָעָתְךָ נָתַתִּי לְךָ אֶת הַשַּׁבָּת
that perhaps I gave you the Shabbos for your harm?"
Since it is so far off
that they should keep Shabbos properly,
that we have not yet merited to keep,
one Shabbos according to its halachah.
"I gave it to you only for your good."
For in truth, as regards punishment,
one can come to desecrating Shabbos,
Only as regards its being called
one Shabbos according to its halachah"
on the part of all of Klal Yisrael,
through which they will be redeemed,
וְאֵימָתַי אַתְּ נוֹתֵן לָנוּ שָׂכָר וְכוּלֵּי
"And when will You give us reward?" etc.,
I will give it to you," etc.
This is "And it will be, ekev,"
which refers to the days of Mashiach;
that is, this is part of the reward of a mitzvah,
וְעָשִׂיתִי אֵת אֲשֶׁר בְּחוּקַּי תֵּלֵכוּ וְגוֹמֵר
"And I will bring it about that you walk in My statutes," etc.
And that is why it says afterward,
from the side of Hashem Yisbarach.
And whatever Hashem Yisbarach gives from His hand,
לֹא יָבֹא מִזֶּה רָעָה חַס וְשָׁלוֹם
no evil, chas v'shalom, will come from it,
nor the accusation of the yetzer hara;
and the eating will be in holiness,
and drink of the wine I have mixed."
which is a day that is entirely Shabbos;
and they are like the addition to Shabbos.
will be the preparation to receive the holiness
like the lighting of the menorah
which one lights during the addition to Shabbos.
And afterward there will be days
שֶׁאֵין בָּהֶם לֹא זְכוּת וְלֹא חוֹבָה
in which there is neither merit nor obligation.
So too we find in the Gemara (Bechoros 44b)
שֶׁנִּדְרַשׁ הַפָּסוּק שֶׁבְּפָרָשָׁה זוֹ (דְּבָרִים ז, יד)
that the pasuk in this parashah (Devarim 7:14) is expounded:
"There will not be among you a barren man":
that your prayer will not be barren
that is, the voice of Torah and the voice of prayer.
When you make yourself like an animal."
וְהוּא עַל דֶּרֶךְ שֶׁאָמְרוּ (חוּלִּין ה, ב)
This is along the lines of what they said (Chullin 5b):
and make themselves like an animal";
that everything is from Hashem Yisbarach,
and nothing at all is from his own effort.
וּכְמוֹ שֶׁאָמַר יַעֲקֹב אָבִינוּ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם (בְּרֵאשִׁית מח, טו)
As Yaakov Avinu, alav hashalom, said (Bereishis 48:15):
from my beginning until this day";
he recognized that all the effort
And on Shabbos a person merits
that everything is from Hashem Yisbarach;
וּכְמוֹ שֶׁכָּתַב בַּזֹּהַר הַקָּדוֹשׁ (חֵלֶק ב פח, א)
as written in the holy Zohar (II 88a):
in the three sanctities of Shabbos.
And when one recognizes the power of the Giver,
that everything is from Hashem Yisbarach,
which come from the aspect of Mazala and Atika.
And when it is from Hashem Yisbarach,
the accusation of the yetzer hara,
וּכְמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ (בְּרֵאשִׁית רַבָּה רֵישׁ פָּרָשָׁה יא)
as they said (Bereishis Rabbah, beginning of 11):
בִּרְכַּת ה׳ הִיא תַעֲשִׁיר (מִשְׁלֵי י, כב)
"'The blessing of Hashem, it makes rich' (Mishlei 10:22):
'and He adds no sorrow with it'";
that is, the sorrow of the yetzer hara;
and as it will be in the days of Mashiach,
"And it will be, ekev, you will hearken":
the reward will be that you will hearken,
And on Shabbos, when one also merits
to recognize that it is from Hashem Yisbarach,
therefore we say at all the meals (Tehillim 23:1):
"Hashem is my shepherd, I shall not lack."
Since one recognizes that Hashem is the shepherd,
there is then no fear of the yetzer hara,
וְכֵן נִדְרַשׁ בַּזֹּהַר הַקָּדוֹשׁ (חֵלֶק א מח, ב)
So too the holy Zohar (I 48b) expounds
"On the day that Hashem gives you rest
from your sorrow and from your trembling,"
as referring to the day of Shabbos;
for then a Jew has rest
from the sorrow of the yetzer hara,
means from the agitation of the yetzer hara
the yetzer tov against the yetzer hara";
that everything is from Hashem Yisbarach.
That is why it is written "on the day that He gives rest,"
and not simply "when He gives rest":
for it refers to the day of Shabbos.
